deities: Lord Shiva (Babulnath — 'Lord of the Babul tree')

history.summary: An ancient Shiva temple on Babulnath hill near Girgaum Chowpatty (Charni Road), South Mumbai. Legend holds that a 12th-century temple consecrated under King Bhimdev of the Shilahara dynasty was destroyed by invaders, its idols buried; in the 1700s a cowherd named Babul noticed his cow Kapila pouring milk over a buried spot, and a Swayambhu Shivling (natural black-stone lingam) was unearthed there. The present temple was built in 1890 by the Gujarati community with Maharaja Sayajirao Gaikwad of Baroda, on land that the Parsi community contested in court until the late 1800s (the courts ruled for the temple). Devotees climb about 80–110 steps (a ₹1 lift is available); the shrine draws crowds on Mondays, in the month of Shravan, and on Mahashivratri. Coordinates are from a full-address geocode match (Girgaon, Mumbai 400006).

town_description: Mumbai is the capital of Maharashtra and India's financial and entertainment capital, spread across seven islands on the Konkan coast along the Arabian Sea. Home to well over 12 million people, it blends colonial-era landmarks with one of the country's densest clusters of historic temples and pilgrim sites. It is connected nationally and internationally through Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, two major railway zones, and an extensive suburban rail and road network.
